statement: The cued base's loop hazard at T 0.6 is set by the problem and by how far the text in context has carried the solution, not by how self-similar that text is: under truncated low-temperature sampling a stuck model locks into a repeat at a roughly steady rate per token (2610.24715), so early zlib compressibility tracks loops only because hard, enumeration-heavy problems both compress well and stay stuck longer, and RL's prefix rescues the base because it carries a sound solution further, whatever its self-similarity.
why_strongest: Each measured value in tests.json compares different problems or different authors, so a hazard set by the problem explains all three. Test k2 (0.67) compares loopers with non-loopers on different problems. Test k3 (0.63) compares base and RL openings, whose styles differ anyway. In the best-controlled test, k4, prefix kind is held fixed inside the hard 78-problem pool, and compressibility nearly stops predicting cap hits: 0.56, against the theory's 0.66. The account fits the items the theory lists as conflicts: excess cap hits in RL's longest quartile (knowledge-9e4147), and base cap hits falling on problems that are long for RL too (result-5de032). It also fits the K arms (knowledge-1497e8). The RL prefix gives 48 finishes and 41 right answers, so the prefix's content carries the solution forward. The base's own prefix, cut from a trajectory that later looped, does worse than a fresh restart (23 finishes against 38), because it is a stuck path. The lock result in 2610.24715 supplies the per-token mechanism without a dose-response on the history.

tests.experiment: On the 78-problem K pool, restricted to problems where the RL-prefix continuation's opening text is at least as compressible as the own-prefix continuation's: how much more often does the RL-prefix arm finish than the own-prefix arm?
tests.recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_rl.jsonl, s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_own.jsonl and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/K_rl.jsonl (all rln4_gen rows). Define ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')) (Python zlib, level 9), and use the stored text field as it is. For each problem_index present in both modal_k-01 K_rl and K_own: take the row with the lowest sample in each file. Drop the problem if either text has len < 3000 characters. rR = ratio(modal K_rl text[:3000]); rO = ratio(K_own text[:3000]). Keep the problem only if rR <= rO. finish_rl = mean of (cap_hit == false) over the modal_k-01 K_rl row and, if one exists, the lowest-sample base_rl-02 K_rl row of the same problem_index (so 0, 0.5 or 1). finish_own = 1 if the K_own row has cap_hit == false, else 0. Statistic: mean over kept problems of (finish_rl - finish_own). Report the number of kept problems and how many of them have a base_rl-02 row.
tests.unit: difference in fraction of problems finished
tests.theory_should_say: The theory says the base finishes from RL's prefix because that text is less self-similar, so where RL's text is as self-similar as the base's own, the advantage should vanish (about 0.0 to 0.05). The rival says RL's prefix helps because it carries the solution further, so it keeps most of the overall +0.32 advantage (about 0.25).

tests.experiment: Among the cued base's rule-A loops at T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, does a more compressible opening bring the loop onset earlier (rank correlation of opening compressibility with onset position)?
tests.recipe: File iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (run_cell rows). Keep rows with loop_A == true and onset_A_char present and >= 4000; drop all other rows. For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:3000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:3000].encode('utf-8')) (Python zlib, level 9). Statistic: Spearman rank correlation between s and onset_A_char over the kept rows (scipy.stats.spearmanr, average ranks for ties). Report the number of kept rows.
tests.theory_should_say: The theory says the hazard at a position grows with how self-similar the text so far is, so a more compressible opening should lock earlier, a positive rho of about 0.25 to 0.35. The rival says that once the problem has the model stuck, the lock comes at a steady per-token rate, so onset is nearly independent of how compressible the opening is (about 0.05).
